one_liner: Educational from-scratch C++ CNN inference engine plus CUDA int8 GEMM; beats cuBLAS only in its slow NN layout.
what_it_does: A small C++20 inference engine for edge-sized CNNs (MNIST, keyword spotting, visual wake words): own tensors, im2col+sgemm convolution, a NEON depthwise kernel, int8 post-training quantization with SDOT, and a liveness-based arena so the forward pass allocates nothing. Models come from a PyTorch exporter in a custom text-header + binary-blob format; the API is Model::load(path) then run(input). An optional CUDA backend holds a ladder of hand-written int8 GEMMs (naive to WMMA+shared memory), Triton equivalents and fused fp32 convolution kernels benchmarked against cuBLAS and cuDNN.
how_it_is_fast: CPU: im2col lowering to a BLAS sgemm (Apple Accelerate, which reaches the AMX unit), bias+ReLU fusion, load-time pre-transposed Linear weights, and passing 1x1 convolutions straight to sgemm without im2col. GPU int8 GEMM: WMMA tensor-core fragments with shared-memory tile staging and a 32x32 output tile per warp (four accumulators). GPU conv: direct convolution with fused bias/ReLU epilogue and filters staged in shared memory.
when_to_use: Learning or teaching how an inference engine is built: every fast path keeps a reference kernel, and the README documents each optimization step and three subtle correctness bugs
Small batch-1 edge CNNs on Apple Silicon where you want a tiny dependency-free engine and accept 1.0-0.6x of ONNX Runtime speed
Studying the int8 GEMM optimization ladder on Ada GPUs (dp4a, WMMA, staging, Triton tile/pipeline ablations)
Tiny fp32 conv layers (3-channel stem, 1x1 pointwise, depthwise) at batch 1 on GPU, where its fused kernels timed faster than cuDNN back-to-back (not yet re-timed without host cost)
when_not_to_use: Any production int8 GEMM: cuBLAS in TN layout is 1.6x-4.5x faster than its best kernel at every size from 256 to 4096
When you need speed over ONNX Runtime on CPU: it ties on the dense MNIST model and is 1.3-1.7x slower on depthwise models
int8 for latency on Apple Silicon: its int8 path is 1.5-6x slower than its own fp32 path (74 vs 49 us MNIST, 1426 vs 240 us VWW)
Models beyond the 11 supported ops (Conv2d, depthwise, Linear, ReLU, pooling, Add, Softmax, Flatten, quantize/dequantize) or anything not NCHW
Mature dependencies: 3 commits, 0 stars, single author

integration.dependencies: a BLAS sgemm (Accelerate on Apple, else a blocked fallback) and pthreads; optional CUDA toolkit with cuBLAS and cuDNN for the GPU backend; uv/Python for export and benchmark tools
integration.min_toolchain: C++20, CMake 3.20; CUDA C++17 for the GPU backend (sm_89 default)
integration.platforms: macOS/Apple Silicon is the measured target (NEON, SDOT probed at configure time); other platforms use a scalar/blocked fallback; CUDA on NVIDIA Ada
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; Model::run writes into a per-model arena and ops share a process-wide singleton ThreadPool, so use one Model per thread at most and do not call set_threads concurrently

gotchas: The headline 2.09x/1.26x/1.24x over cuBLAS is against cuBLAS called with row-major B (NN), a slow path; the author retracts it in the same README
GPU timings in the first tables are back-to-back launches that include about 10 us of host cost per cuBLAS call at small n
Tensor-core kernels require dimensions that are multiples of 16 (wmma) or 64 (staged); ragged shapes fall back to CUDA-core kernels
Author states run-to-run noise of about +/-10% on an unpinned laptop; CPU differences under 15% are ties
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only to learn; for a real mobile CNN runtime use MNN, and for fast CPU matmul in LLM inference use llamafile tinyBLAS or T-MAC.
verified_claims_summary: On an RTX 4090 its best int8 WMMA kernel beat cuBLAS called in NN layout up to n=1024 (2.09x at 256) and lost from 2048 up, while cuBLAS in its proper TN layout is 1.6-4.5x faster at every size. On an Apple M4 Pro (CMake Release, -O3, Accelerate sgemm) the CPU engine measured 49/110/240 us vs ONNX Runtime's 48/67/184 us on the three MLPerf-Tiny-style models, so it is not faster on CPU.
status_note: Active as of September 2026 but a single-author learning project (3 commits, 0 stars); MIT-licensed and small enough to read or vendor, not to depend on.
